title: An element of a local projective module lies in a free summand
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring (a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal), let $P$ be a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and let $x\in P$. There exist submodules $G,H\subseteq P$ such that $P=G\oplus H$, $x\in G$, and $G$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Here $P=G\oplus H$ means that every element of $P$ has a unique expression $g+h$ with $g\in G$ and $h\in H$. No finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $P$ or $G$.

proof.text: By the direct-summand characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], identify $P$ with a submodule of a free module $F$ and take an $R$-linear map $\pi:F\to P$ restricting to $1_P$. Then $F=P\oplus\ker\pi$, since $f=\pi(f)+(f-\pi(f))$ uniquely. If $x=0$, take $G=0$, with empty basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $H=P$. Assume $x\ne0$ and regard $\pi$ also as an endomorphism of $F$.

Apply [lem-trf-minimal-support-fixed-vector-coordinates] to $F,x,\pi$; its hypothesis $\pi(x)=x$ holds because $x\in P$. Obtain the basis $\mathcal B$, its finite support $e_1,\ldots,e_n$, the irredundant coefficients $a_i$, $T$, and the expansions $y_i=\pi(e_i)=\sum_j b_{ij}e_j+t_i$. In particular $y_i\in P$, $x=\sum_i a_i y_i$, and $a_j=\sum_i a_i b_{ij}$.

The ring $R$ is local and the tuple $a_i$ is irredundant, so [lem-trf-local-irredundant-relation-matrix] applies to $B=(b_{ij})$ and the relations just obtained. It gives an inverse of $B$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-block-basis-replacement] to the same ambient basis, support, vectors $y_i$, coefficients $b_{ij}$, and tails $t_i\in T$. It supplies a basis of $G=\sum_i R y_i$ and the decomposition $F=G\oplus T$.

Since every $y_i$ lies in $P$, $G\subseteq P$. Put $H=P\cap T$. For $p\in P$, the unique expansion $p=g+t$ in $F=G\oplus T$ has $t=p-g\in P\cap T=H$. The uniqueness in $F$ proves uniqueness in $P$, hence $P=G\oplus H$. Step 2 gives $x=\sum_i a_i y_i\in G$, and the basis of $G$ from step 3 makes $G$ free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This also covers arbitrary ambient rank; the zero case was handled in step 1.
